decisions.rationale: Charizard-Mega-Y + Garchomp lead: Drought-boosted Heat Wave is foes-only so it pressures the Staraptor/Raichu lead without touching my partner, and Garchomp is flat-out immune to Mega Raichu's No Guard Zap Cannon (their only para/win-con vs my special attackers) while outspeeding base Staraptor and threatening Rock Slide/Stomping Tantrum. Backs cover the two mons that beat me in G1: Kingambit resists Fairy 0.25x, is immune to Psychic, and Iron Head/Kowtow Cleave near-OHKOs Sylveon and Farigiraf (TR mode), while Basculegion's Adaptability Wave Crash is a guaranteed OHKO on Arcanine-Hisui through Focus Sash even in sun and still crushes Sylveon. Basculegion Aqua Jet (4x, Adaptability + Mystic Water) does 47.5-94.1% and consumes nothing of the Sash (no KO from full), then Kingambit Sucker Punch adds 30.2-57.1% — combined 78-151%, so the median roll kills Arcanine before it ever moves, sidestepping the guaranteed Flare Blitz KO on Kingambit. Iron Head on Sylveon was tempting (78-152%) but Kingambit is the slowest thing on the field at normal priority and would likely faint first; Wave Crash is halved in my own sun and resolves after Arcanine. Worst case (Arcanine Protects) I only lose tempo, not a Pokemon.

reflections.summary: Won Game 2 (6 turns) and series 2-0 with clean piloting (0 errors). Preview plan suited opponent's actual 4: they benched Whimsicott (Prankster Tailwind/Encore) and Floette-Eternal (Mega Fairy) and brought Charizard-Mega-Y/Garchomp/Basculegion/Kingambit. Our 4 - Staraptor (Tailwind/Intimidate) + Raichu (Fake Out/Lightning Rod) + Sylveon (Pixilate Hyper Voice) + Arcanine-H (Rock Head Head Smash/Extreme Speed/Sash) - directly answered that: Tailwind vs sun, Fake Out vs Garchomp Rock Slide, spread Hyper Voice super-effective vs Garchomp and chunking Kingambit/Basculegion, Head Smash super-effective vs Charizard-Y and Extreme Speed for Kingambit. Mega choice was correct: neither Staraptorite nor Raichunite-Y was evolved - base utility (Intimidate, Fake Out, speed) mattered more than Mega power and preserved tempo. Piloting executed plan: T1 Fake Out flinch Garchomp secured Tailwind despite Staraptor lost to Heat Wave, T2 pivot Sylveon for Arcanine, T3-5 Hyper Voice spread + Protect + Extreme Speed cleaned Garchomp/Kingambit/Basculegion, T6 Head Smash finished re-entered Charizard-Y. Series win = favorable preview matchup + error-free tempo control; no between-game adjustment backfired (1-0 lead held).
reflections.adjustment: No major change needed vs this Charizard-Y sun + Garchomp/Kingambit/Basculegion offense - keep same 4 and keep Mega unevolved for utility. In a future series expect opponent to re-introduce benched Whimsicott Tailwind war and Floette-Eternal Mega Fairy (Light of Ruin) - if so, prioritize keeping Arcanine-H Sash intact for Fairy/Charizard and consider Sylveon + Raichu lead to pressure Fairy while still contesting Tailwind, don't force early Mega evolution.
reflections.notebook: Top-cut sun offense player. Tendency: lead Charizard-Y + Garchomp, Mega evolve Charizard T1 to set sun, play Heat Wave spread + Protect stall, Garchomp Rock Slide spread. Backline is Kingambit (Chople, Sucker Punch) + Basculegion (Adaptability Aqua Jet) for priority cleanup. Willing to bench usual Prankster Whimsicott Tailwind/Encore and Floette-Eternal Mega Fairy to go 4 attackers vs Tailwind/Fake Out teams (did so in G2). Counter durable: Fake Out Garchomp to guarantee Tailwind, Pixilate Hyper Voice pressures entire core, Extreme Speed answers low Kingambit through Sucker Punch, Rock Head Head Smash answers Charizard-Y without Sash break.

reflections.summary: Lost the game and the series to the same pattern as Game 1: I traded pieces one-at-a-time and ended up in a 1-vs-2. The preview plan was half-right — Mega Charizard-Y's turn-1 Heat Wave again cleanly removed Staraptor before it could Mega (denying Contrary Close Combat) and chipped Raichu to 7% — but the other three brought (Garchomp, Basculegion, Kingambit) all matched up badly into the surviving backline. Garchomp's Rock Slide missed the Focus-Sash Arcanine-Hisui on turn 2, so the sash never broke and Arcanine stayed a full-power Head Smash threat all game; Garchomp then died to Sylveon's Pixilate Hyper Voice (Life Orb chip + spread Fairy). Kingambit was dead weight for the third time: at 81 Speed it only ever gets Sucker Punch, which failed into Arcanine's Protect, and it absorbed two Hyper Voices before dying to a resisted Extreme Speed. Basculegion, my one real Arcanine answer, had its Aqua Jet halved by my own Drought, so it needed two turns to get Arcanine to 25% and was picked off by Hyper Beam first. That left a lone Mega Zard forced in against a healthy-enough Arcanine, which auto-OHKOs it with Head Smash — the loss was locked in a turn before it happened. Piloting was clean on paper (0 errors, correct Protect on the Head Smash turn), but the structural errors were team-level: two Fairy-vulnerable slow bodies, and a sun setter that actively weakens the Water attacker I needed. The between-game adjustment (same lead, Kingambit brought again) did not help and effectively backfired — it repeated the exact Game 1 failure mode.
reflections.adjustment: Bench Kingambit entirely — it has now been a non-factor in every game and only feeds Sylveon's spread Fairy damage. Bring a fourth that can pressure Arcanine-Hisui and Sylveon without fighting my own sun, and stop pairing two Fairy-weak/slow bodies with Sylveon on the field. Keep Mega Charizard-Y purely as a turn-1 tool: Heat Wave to remove Staraptor before it Megas and chip Raichu, then get it off the field immediately and never let it end up as the last mon, since Arcanine outspeeds it and Head Smash is a guaranteed OHKO. Answer Arcanine with Solar Beam/Ground damage rather than sun-halved Water, and when Basculegion is needed as the Water answer, either delay Mega evolution or accept that Aqua Jet needs a chip partner. Break the Focus Sash and finish in the same turn — spread damage first, single-target kill second — instead of chipping across turns and letting Protect reset tempo. Above all, stop the greedy single-target trade pattern: preserve two healthy bodies through the Tailwind turns and let their Tailwind expire (it ran out on turn 4 both times) before committing to KO attempts.

DURABLE TENDENCIES (3 games observed): Leads Staraptor + Raichu every single game — never deviated. Backline has always been Sylveon + Arcanine-Hisui; Farigiraf and their Kingambit have NEVER been brought (but assume Trick Room/Armor Tail is possible in a fresh series and never rely solely on priority). Turn 1 they commit Staraptor to Tailwind rather than Protect, even into an obvious Fire lead — Staraptor is expendable and has died turn 1 repeatedly without ever Mega evolving. Raichu's Fake Out targets my physical attacker, not the special threat, and Raichu has never actually Mega evolved yet. Arcanine-Hisui spams Head Smash freely (Rock Head, no recoil) and uses Protect on turns where a priority/Water attack is obvious. Sylveon will fire Hyper Beam to guarantee a KO and accept the recharge — that recharge turn is a free turn for me. Their Tailwind expires after turn 4; games are decided by whether I still have two healthy bodies at that point.

SPEED/THREAT FACTS: Arcanine-H (raw 121-156) outspeeds Mega Zard (135). Mega Raichu (165-200) outspeeds my entire team. Intimidate on the Staraptor lead drops both my physical leads a stage.

DAMAGE (sun): Arcanine-H Head Smash — Mega Zard 226-331% (auto OHKO), Basculegion 60-87%, Kingambit 16-34%; Flare Blitz OHKOs Kingambit from full; Extreme Speed — Basculegion IMMUNE (Ghost), Kingambit 0.5x. Basculegion Aqua Jet into Arcanine-H 47.5-94% (halved by my own sun). Kingambit Iron Head into Sylveon 78-152%, Sucker Punch into Arcanine 30-57%.

STANDING LESSONS: (1) Mega Zard must never share the field with a healthy Arcanine-Hisui and must never be the last mon — Head Smash is a guaranteed OHKO. (2) Removing Raichu/Staraptor turn 1 with Heat Wave works, but killing the lead is not enough; the Sylveon + Arcanine back pair is what actually wins their games. (3) My own Drought halves my Water moves — the Zard/Basculegion pairing is anti-synergistic against the mon Water is meant to answer. (4) Focus Sash is dead once chipped: chip and finish inside the same turn. (5) Kingambit (81 Spe) has contributed nothing in three games — Sucker Punch fails into Protect/Arcanine's non-attacking turns, and it just eats Hyper Voice; bench it. (6) Every loss came from collapsing into a 1-vs-2+; trade evenly, survive Tailwind, avoid stacking Fairy-vulnerable bodies against Sylveon.
